acceptance.criterion_verbatim: DECIMAL DTYPES per the SILVER-DTYPE law (the Travis-Decimal specimen is the pointer). Float-coerced money is the defect this criterion exists to catch.
acceptance.invocation: pyarrow.parquet.read_table(run1/data.parquet).schema type census + element-wise Decimal value tie vs the source xlsx
acceptance.output_evidence: EMITTED SCHEMA: 13 decimal128 columns, 6 date32 columns, 77 string columns, and ZERO float/double columns -- the float-coerced-money defect is absent by construction, not by assertion. Decimal columns: basis_points, flat_fee, flat_fee_1, basis_points_1, lower_range, upper_range, upper_range_1, lower_range_1, account_allocation, account_market_value, portfolio_group_market_value, cash_market_value, cash_allocation. Conversion is via str() (shortest round-trip repr), NEVER Decimal(float), so no binary noise enters a money column; a value exceeding pinned precision/scale RAISES rather than rounding (PrecisionError). THE GUARD IS EXERCISED, NOT THEORETICAL: it fired on the first run against account_allocation 0.0371002078317068 and blocked the build -- the arithmetic in my precision check was wrong (I used len(digits)+|exp| instead of len(digits)+exp+scale); the data was fine and the guard caught my bug. VALUE TIE: account_market_value compared element-wise over all 30,577 rows against the source cast to Decimal -- 0 mismatches; sum 8,459,429,469.8235 both sides. Standardization changed TYPES, not VALUES. Specimen account_allocation[1] = 0.193176246453041000000000 (exact Decimal, not a float repr). DELIBERATELY NOT COERCED: the six '* Split %' columns stay string because they carry the sentinel 'No <Role> Split % Value Assigned' mixed with numerals -- typing them numeric would require deciding what the sentinel MEANS, a null-meaning judgment that Rule 17 assigns to gold.
acceptance.denominator: 96 emitted columns typed (92 vendor + 4 provenance); 30,577 of 30,577 rows compared on the value tie

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: NO FIELD LOSS: the emitted column set is the bronze column set. Print both counts -- equality is the criterion, not 'looks complete.'
acceptance.invocation: manifest.json columns_in vs columns_out, cross-read against the emitted parquet's own schema width
acceptance.output_evidence: BRONZE COLUMNS = 92. EMITTED VENDOR COLUMNS = 92. EQUAL. The emitted table is 96 columns total = 92 vendor + 4 provenance (_source_key, _source_as_of, _schema_version, _row_sha256) -- additive per the estate PROVENANCE_COLS pattern, nothing removed. Column names are mangled mechanically (lowercase, non-alphanumeric -> underscore, collision-suffixed) and the COMPLETE original->emitted mapping is written into the manifest, so the vendor header is reconstructable from the artifact alone. The vendor header is PINNED: a partition whose header does not match the pinned 92 raises SchemaDriftError naming the missing and unknown columns, rather than silently re-binding a mangled name to different data.
acceptance.denominator: 92 of 92 bronze columns accounted for; 96 of 96 emitted columns enumerated

mutant.description: Two independent mutants were run rather than asserted. (2) DECIMAL PRECISION GUARD: the guard was not hand-triggered; it fired on its own during the first real build against account_allocation 0.0371002078317068 and refused to write.
mutant.expected: (1) the mutated file must compare UNEQUAL. (2) a value that does not fit the pinned precision/scale must RAISE, never silently round.
mutant.observed: (1) the 1-byte mutation DID flip the verdict to unequal -- the comparison is real. (2) PrecisionError raised and halted the build; investigation showed the DATA was valid and MY precision arithmetic was wrong (len(digits)+|exp| instead of len(digits)+exp+scale). Fixed, re-run clean. The guard caught an author bug on its first live exercise, which is the strongest evidence it is not decorative.
